plan.flow: Responsive feedlot operations web app: staff sign in, then use one permission-aware yard workspace for importing procurement and receiving data, tracing lots and pens, managing feed and inventory, planning and recording feeding, and reviewing performance. Service-returned permissions control navigation, records, actions, and exports. The delivery brief documents the proposed solution and demo.

screens.title: Sign in
states: Authentication error returned by the sign-in service
Successful sign-in routes to the returned landing page
screens.prompt: Create the email-and-password sign-in page for Range Ledger. Keep the page to the brand mark and words above one centred panel no wider than 440 px; inside the panel put the heading “Sign in”, one sentence “Use your work account to open your yard.”, then labelled Email and Password fields and the single primary button “Sign in”. Use believable entered-state examples only in the validation state, not as the normal page. Submit credentials to the sign-in service; show its authentication error in the panel without losing the email, and on success go to the service-returned landing page with that user’s returned permissions. Responsive phone, tablet and desktop; no header, footer, illustration or extra navigation.

screens.title: Yard
states: Session expiry or protected-request HTTP 401: clear authenticated page data and return to Sign in

screens.prompt: At the top, a plain header carries the brand words “Range Ledger” beside a small square mark with a white “R”; the shared menu sits to the right of the brand and keeps this order: Yard, Imports, Allocations, Lots, Inventory, Feed outlook, Rations, Feed plans, Feeding, Reports, Feed-to-gain, Profitability, Sample data, Delivery brief. On the far right, show Maya Chen’s real photograph on the left of her name and the role “Yard manager”; hide menu items and actions the signed-in user’s returned permissions do not allow. Let “360 active head” be the first, largest figure, with the service-returned yard context; directly below show the returned yard summary—average ADG 3.02 lb/day, average cost of gain $1.12/lb, total feed cost $82,060—and unavailable values if source data is missing. Follow with a dense sortable lot-performance table, not metric cards: L-2407, L-2409, L-2411 and L-2413, head, ADG, FCR, cost of gain, feed cost and energy; provide a measure selector that re-ranks best and worst lots. Add a compact inventory balance of 137,400 lb, today’s planned delivery of 8,384 lb and the latest weight/feeding activity from the shared dated event list. For activity rows show real photographs of the named staff—Eli Navarro, Rosa Alvarez, Maya Chen, Tomas Reed and Omar Diaz—not illustrated avatars. Use an orderly white worklist, plain bar, soft-cornered surfaces and restrained status chips. On wide screens place the headline and yard summary above a full-width table; on phones stack sections and keep controls touch-sized. Leave breathing room around the dense table; no three-card row.

screens.title: Delivery brief
screens.prompt: At the top, a plain header carries the brand words “Range Ledger” beside a small square mark with a white “R”; the shared menu sits to the right of the brand and keeps this order: Yard, Imports, Allocations, Lots, Inventory, Feed outlook, Rations, Feed plans, Feeding, Reports, Feed-to-gain, Profitability, Sample data, Delivery brief. On the far right, show Maya Chen’s real photograph on the left of her name and the role “Yard manager”; hide menu items and actions the signed-in user’s returned permissions do not allow. Create “Delivery brief” as a concise, editorial delivery overview for the Red Mesa Yard feedlot web app. Start with the proposed solution and one real product description, then a labelled architecture diagram: responsive browser UI → sign-in and permission service → yard operations services → documented mock procurement/receiving adapter and feed/inventory/report services. Include a prominent product-specific demo entry action “Open yard demo” to the Yard page. Follow with a “Prompts used” section showing the actual project brief (“Build a responsive feedlot operations web app with permission-aware procurement imports, lot-to-pen traceability, feeding, inventory, ration planning, forecasts and authorized reporting”) and the UI prompt principle (“Draw each page as a finished responsive staff worklist with returned-service data and role-gated actions”). Add a testing and validation overview covering sign-in/401 clearing, permissions and exports, repeated-import allocation conflicts, multi-lot feed validation, stock errors and timed-out saves. Include challenges (stale head counts, traceability conflicts, separating actual wastage from delivered feed), a candid production-readiness assessment (mock adapter and service contracts still need production integration, security review and operational validation), and a go-to-market analysis for feedlot operators, phased onboarding and measurable pilot outcomes. Vary section rhythm with a narrow text column, diagram and dense checklist; no testimonial carousel, three equal cards or oversized centered hero.

system.digest: Use 4px corners on panels, fields, and buttons. Edge panels with a 1px rule and no shadow; use an 8px spacing rhythm with a 4px half-step and 24px desktop panel padding, reduced to 16px on phones. Set first-level headings to 32px/650, second-level to 24px/600, and third-level to 18px/600; body text is 16px with 24px leading. Keep table rows 48px tall, at least 56px on phones, divided by a single 1px horizontal rule. Make primary buttons solid and secondary buttons outlined; fields have a visible 2px focus outline, and all three are 44px tall or 48px on phones. Show each state with its own small colored indicator and sentence-case text, never color alone. Crop operational photos to 4:3 and portraits to 1:1; reuse the same person’s exact image and crop wherever repeated. Separate major groups with open space and a full-width 2px rule, keeping ordinary row rules at 1px.

motion.signature: The feeding-sequence track fills from left to right as its row enters view (`animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% entry 55%; animation-duration: 420ms; animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`).
motion.ambient: Only while a real operational state is actively updating, its small status dot breathes from 0.82 to 0.86 opacity on an 8s infinite cycle (`animation: live-breathe 8s cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) infinite`).
